observations.code_quote: 1. **Read the vendor's changelog** (the source's `api_docs_url`) and list what changed between the currently supported version(s) and the new one: renamed/removed fields, changed pagination, new required headers, changed webhook payloads, or a field the source reads becoming opt-in behind a new query parameter (a field returned by default in the old version now empty unless requested — restore it by adding that parameter on the new version's request path). Verification is docs-only — there are no stored credentials and no live-sync harness, so the docs are the sole source of truth for what each version serves. When the vendor's docs page renders client-side and comes back as an empty shell, read its machine-readable mirror (an `llms.txt`, a `sitemap.md`, or the same path with a `.md` suffix) rather than treating the version as undocumented. A Postman-published docs site carries `ownerId` and `publishedId` meta tags; `https://documenter.gw.postman.com/api/collections/<ownerId>/<publishedId>?versionTag=latest` returns the whole collection as JSON, changelog included in `info.description`. The reverse also happens: a `.md` mirror can be a stub that links to a spec without the endpoint, while the rendered HTML page carries the full request line and schema, so read the HTML before concluding the docs are missing. When the vendor publishes only one version-blind spec for the current version and no changelog, diff it against an archived copy (the Wayback Machine's CDX index lists snapshots; the `id_` form returns the raw file, sometimes still gzip-encoded) and check which label that copy names: differences it shows span every version between that copy and now, so do not attribute them to the new label alone. For a GraphQL vendor that serves a schema per version, validate the source's exact query strings against each version's SDL (for example with `graphql-core`'s `validate`): it names every removed field a query selects, and it settles changelog entries that only say a removal is "planned". This is also the evidence the gate above runs on.
